entry.dc:title: Surface mining, solid waste diposal combined at Pennsylvania operation
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: Aloe Coal Co of Imperial, Pa, is producing 60,000 t/mo of coal by surface mining. In order to reduce cost of mining as well as to speed up land reclamation the company entered into a contractual arrangement with the City of Pittsburgh, whereby the former is paid for picking up an average of 700 tpd of solid refuse, transporting it over a distance of 18 mi, spreading and compacting it in mined- out open pits. In order to prevent water pollution, the refuse is placed over an impervious clay lining.

entry.dc:title: Mining guidebook
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: This annual feature summarizes recent developments in techniques of- mine development; continuous- longwall, and conventional mining; roof control; haulage and hoisting; mine ventilation; mine drainage and acid water treatment; surface mining; coal preparation and unit- train loading; maintenance engineering; efficient power designs; purchasing and warehousing; and safety.

entry.dc:title: Survey of crawler dozers and wheel frontend loaders
entry.dc:creator: JONES DC
entry.dc:description: Originally considered as '%'service'%' machines in strip mining of coal, these tractor units have experienced rapid growth in recent years in both application and size, even to the extent of replacing older type machines. Paper reviews the types of commercially available machines and cites in tabulated form selected data on crawler tractors and rubber wheel front end loaders used in surface mining.

entry.dc:title: EXCAVATORS
entry.dc:creator: RUMFELT H
entry.dc:description: The development, capabilities and relative merits of the big excavators used for surface and strip mining are surveyed in this article. Along with his discussion of shovels, draglines, and bucketwheel excavators, the author considers the future of these machines and of surface mining itself. He also discusses the possible influence of environmental regulation on surface mining and points out some improvements which would make surface excavators more economical to operate.

entry.dc:title: Environmental side effects of rising industrial output, (Studies in Social and Economic Process)
entry.dc:creator: VAN TASSEL ED AJ
entry.dc:description: The complex of problems involved in dealing with environmental pollution was the subject of a research seminar held at Hofstra University, School of Business. Some of the problems considered are- % water pollution and expanding production in the steel, paper, chemical, and petroleum industries; nonindustrial water pollution; thermal pollution; disposal of atomic wastes; air pollution and the expanding consumption of fuels; solid waste disposal problems; harmful side effects of pesticide use; and the environmental effects of surface mining and mineral waste generation.

entry.dc:title: Mining and ecology in the arid environment, Proceedings, Mar 22- 27 1970, Tucson, Ariz
entry.dc:creator: PETERS ED WC
entry.dc:description: Proceedings contains 21 papers discussing following groups of topics- perspectives facing the mining industry in title region from the viewpoint of environmental engineering; air pollution control with emphasis on fumes emission; management of water resources; land reclamation with emphasis on surface mining and tailings disposal; control and design of mining operations; and evaluation of quality environment. Minutes of discussions and bibliographic references are included.

entry.dc:title: PRODUCTION POTENTIAL OF COPPER DEPOSITS ASSOCIATED WITH PERMIAN RED BED FORMATIONS IN TEXAS, OKLAHOMA, AND KANSAS
entry.dc:creator: STROUD RB
entry.prism:publicationName: U S Bur Mines Rep Invest 7422
entry.dc:description: Bureau of Mines studies of copper-bearing Permian red beds, which extend from north-central Texas through western Oklahoma to south- western Kansas, indicate heretofore undefined commercial possibilities for low-grade, medium- volume, surface mining operations. Potential orebodies are indicated containing 0. 5 to 1. 5% copper in zones 6 to 12 in. thick. Cost analysis studies indicate a commercial operation is feasible for a hypothecated 1000 tpd ore mining and milling complex where a maximum of 60 ft of overburden can be removed in mining a seam of shale 12 in. thick containing 1. 2% copper.

entry.dc:title: Planning open pit mines (Open Pit Mining Symposium 1970). Proceedings of the symposium on the theoretical background to the planning of open pit mines with special reference to slope stability, Aug 29- Sept 4 1970, Johannesburg, Republic of South Africa, arranged by the South African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:creator: VAN RENSBURG ED PWJ
entry.dc:description: Proceeding contains twenty- one papers related to optimizing open pit geometry; geological factors significant to the stability of rock slopes; water pressure as factor in the slope theory; methods for calculating stresses and stability of slopes; control for early warning of potential danger and prediction of slope failure by monitoring; blasting in surface mining; and basic principles of open pit equipment selection.

entry.dc:title: COAL, OIL, NATURAL GAS, HELIUM, AND URANIUM IN ARIZONA
entry.dc:creator: PEIRCE HW
entry.dc:description: Brief review of Arizona's geological setting is followed by monographic studies of coal, oil, natural gas, helium, and uranium deposits as well as present state-of- art in exploration and production. Black Mesa coal field, containing some 20 billion t of coal within 1700 ft from the surface is being developed for surface mining of good quality coal to be pipelined to Mojave power plant in Nevada. Oil, natural gas and helium deposits occur in the northeastern Plateau province. Production since 1954 amounted to 9. 3 million bbl of oil, 8. 5 and 5. 5 billion cu ft of naturalgas and helium respectively, but the potential is still largely untested. Uranium ores will need a considerable amount of exploration.

entry.dc:title: TECHNOLOGY AND USE OF LIGNITE
entry.dc:creator: ELDER JL
entry.prism:publicationName: U S Bur Mines Inform Circ 8471
entry.dc:description: Proceedings contains 14 papers discussing-lignite and total energy concept; effect of surface mining on environment; the importance of ash in the combustion of coal; ash fouling and air pollution studies; ash deposition research on Canadian lignites; operational experience with lignite in steam power plants; lignite fly ash utilization; the use of lignite products as plant growth stimulants, and the use of char to improve the physical quality of coke.

entry.dc:title: Medet. Bulgaria's giant porphyry copper- molybdenum kombinat
entry.dc:creator: ARGALL G.
entry.dc:description: After 9 yr of construction and operation, Medet, Bulgaria's largest mine should reach in 1971, its designed yearly capacity of mining and milliong 8 millio n to of ore. Surface porphyry copper- molybdenum mine, located about 70 mi east of Sofia, has reserves claimed to exceed 150 million t of low- grade ore assaying 0. 36% Cu, 0. 0008% Mo, and 1. 0 to 1. 2% S. Surface mining and ore treatment techniques are described. Mill flowsheet is included.

entry.dc:title: How to make explosives do more work
entry.dc:creator: GRANT CH
entry.dc:description: All though explosives have been used as tools in mining for more than a century there is still very little understanding of the way in which this tremendous chemical energy should be employed. Article describes some of the latest techniques developed for the efficient use of explosives and blasting procedures in surface mining.

entry.dc:title: ZWARTKLOOF TO PRODUCE SOON
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: This new fluorspar producer in the Gold Fields of South Africa group is situated approximately 7 mi. to the west of Warmbaths in Transvaal. Initially the ore bodies, estimated to contain 7,000,000 t averaging 13. 7% CaF//2 will be exploited by surface mining, to resort to underground mining at later stages. The ore to be treated by heavy media and flotation is expected to produce concentrates assaying 97% CaF//2, 1. 0% SiO//2, 1. 25% CaCo//3, 0. 02% S and Al//2O//3, Fe//2O//3 and Zn not exceeding 0. 70% total.

entry.dc:title: MULTIPLE SEAM SURFACE MINING
entry.dc:creator: CAMPBELL RA
entry.dc:description: Peabody Coal Company, at its Homestead, Kentucky mine, is recovering coal from three, flat laying seams 2. 5, 6. 0 and 4. 5 ft thick in the same pit at average depths of 50, 120 and 180 ft respectively. Characteristics of the overburden, thickness and parting of seams, available large capacity mining equipment, and market requirements for the coal determine the success of this type of operation.

entry.dc:title: OPERATING EXPERIENCE WITH PORTABLE STONE CRUSHERS IN THE UNITED STATES AND EUROPE,
entry.dc:creator: KOCHANOWSKY BJ
entry.dc:description: Paper emphasizes the advantages of portable crushers in quarrying and surface mining operations, permitting the use of belt conveyors in conjunction with loaders and high capacity motor trucks. Typical installations are described and the economics involved are discussed.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: Surface mining guidebook discusses recent development in the United States in-planning operations; drilling and blasting; overburden removal and equipment used; coal loading; haulage, drainage, augering; and land reclamation.

entry.dc:title: DESIGNING HAUL ROADS FOR ECONOMIC TRUCK PERFORMANCE-- 1
entry.dc:creator: MORGAN BV
entry.dc:description: To determine the most economical type and quantity of trucks for any long distance haulage in earthmoving surface mining, and quarrying operations, empirical relationships can be used to assess the effect on the performance of factors such as haul distance, road grade, maneuvering times, etc. Guidelines for consideration of influence of-- road- , grade and rolling resistance, haul- , length- , entry and exit-, and power- reserve factors, loading area- , waiting- , and dumping-time and altitude are given and discussed.

entry.dc:title: MINING WITH FRONT END LOADERS
entry.dc:creator: NUTTER FB
entry.dc:description: Surface mining has always been dominated by power shovels and draglines, but mobile equipment has supplemented the primary excavator for at least 40 yr. Since World War II, track-or rubber- tire mounted front end loaders have found increasing use in coal mining, and for the last several years, they have been playing a vital role in contour mining. At many operations they arethe main stripping tool.

entry.dc:title: COPPER-MOLYBDENUM MINE NOW IN PRODUCTION
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: Eighteen miles from Peachland, BC, the Brenda mine is now in full production, treating copper ad molybdenum-bearing ore at the rate of 24,000 tpd. Its ore body, about 2800 ft long 1300 ft wide and 900 ft deep is wholly confined to speckled quartz diorite, strongly faulted and fractured and is estimated to contain 177 million t of ore assaying 0. 183% Cu and 0. 049% Mo. Surface mining called for removal of 9 million t of overburden. Milling operations designed to produce 200 tpd of copper-, and 20 to 25 tpd of molybdenum concentrates are described and the flowsheet of the ore treatment process is included. Tailings disposal and water recycling techniques are discussed.

entry.dc:title: RUTILE SECONDARY DEPOSITS OF SIERRA LEONE, WEST AFRICA,
entry.dc:creator: LANG HD
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: Report on geological investigation of deposit, located in southern province of Sierra Leone, carried out in 1968/69. Those alluvial river sediments filling wide, flat valleys on either side of Gbangbama Range have probably originated with archean granat- bearing, gneisses. Present production target of surface mining, followed by magnetic and electrostatic separation of rutile is 100,000 tonnes/yr of concentrates assaying between 95 and 97% of TiO//2. Total reserves are estimated to amount to 12-million tonnes of rutile.

entry.dc:title: ISLAND COPPER PROJECT
entry.dc:creator: PRATT ME
entry.dc:description: Utah Construction & Mining Co's new Island Copper mine is located on Rupert Inlet at the northern end of Vancouver Island. The presently-defined orebody has estimated reserves of 280 million t of copper-molybdenum ore, with an average grade of 0. 52% copper, 0. 029% molybdenum sulfide. Orebody is being developed for surface mining of 33,000 tpd of ore. Annual output will be 230,000 t of copper-, and 1800 t of molybdenum concentrate. Flotation tailings will be disposed of through a submerged pipe line discharging into Rupert Inlet about 2600 ft from the shoreline at a depth in excess of 150 ft.

entry.dc:title: NABALCO PROJECT AT GOVE
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: Bauxite deposit with reserves approximately 250-million t, located at Gove Peninsula, Northern Territory, Australia, is being developed by Nabalco Propr, Ltd. About 11 ft thick in average ore body overlaying a 160 ft high above sea level plateau and capped with laterite is prepared for surface mining to produce 3. 5 million t/yr. Crushed at the mine bauxite will be transported by a 12 m long overland belt-conveyor to treatment plant at Dundas Point port. Details of treatment process, stock piling systems and terminal facilities with loading capacity of 2000tph are given. Nabalco is owned by Swiss Aluminum (70%) and Australian interests.

entry.dc:title: MUSKINGUM. TEST-TUBE FOR FUTURE
entry.dc:creator: HOUSER FN
entry.dc:description: Railroad electrification studies based on technology incorporated in Ohio industrial line of 15 1/2-mi automated electric railroad and large dragline, at surface mining operation of Central Ohio Coal Co southeast of Zanesville, Ohio; 2000-5on train traverses main line with E50 locomotive respondint to speed commands of passive inductors.

entry.dc:title: RECENT ADVANCES IN ENGINEERING SCIENCE, V 4. PROC OF FIFTH TECHNICAL MEETING OF THE SOC OF ENG SCI, HELD OCT 30-NOV 1 1967, HUNTSVILLE, ALA
entry.dc:creator: ERINGEN ED AC
entry.prism:publicationName: Gordon and Breach Sci Publ Inc
entry.dc:description: Proceedings include twenty papers related to the theme of engineering science in space. Subjects cover reactors for outer space, structural problems, plasma experiments in space, microwave deep space communications and space astronomy. Research topics covered include electromagnetic fields, gas dynamics, shock waves, aerodynamics, blunt heat shields, solid mechanics, fatigue of metals, inclusions, n-body problems, guidance, spaceradiators, lunar surface mining, etc.

entry.dc:title: CASE STUDIES OF SURFACE MINING. PROCEEDINGS OF II INTERNATIONAL SURFACE MINING CONFERENCE, MINNEAPOLIS, MINN, SEPT 18-20 1968

entry.prism:publicationName: Am Inst of Min Met Petroleum Engrs New York Ny
